title: Minimum Operations to Make a Uni-Value Grid
summary: Given a grid of size m x n and an integer x, determine the least number of operations needed to make all elements equal by adding or subtracting x.
statement: Given a grid of size m x n and an integer x, determine the least number of operations needed to make all elements equal by adding or subtracting x. If achieving a uni-value grid is impossible, return -1.
constraints: grid is nonempty with at most 100000 cells and x is positive.
One operation adds or subtracts x from one cell.
Return the minimum operations to make every cell equal, or -1 if impossible.
hints: Adding or subtracting x preserves each value’s remainder modulo x, so differing remainders make the task impossible.
After scaling congruent values by x, minimizing absolute distance is a median problem.
Sort values, choose the median, and sum abs(value-median)//x.
The median minimizes total L1 distance, and congruence guarantees every quotient represents an attainable integer number of operations.
editorial: The median minimizes total L1 distance, and congruence guarantees every quotient represents an attainable integer number of operations.
